hardware_enforcement.rationale: B1.4-P7 enforces live branch-protection hardware required contexts for the full terminal privacy proof plane.

b25_ci_topology.rationale: Checkout Code becomes merge-blocking because the throughput topology removed its needs: edges. It previously gated 66 jobs and blocked merges implicitly by starving downstream contexts; those edges transferred no data and serialised the graph. The job and its assertions (adjudicated-SHA check, evidence placement) are unchanged - only the enforcement mechanism moved from an ordering constraint to an explicit required status check, which is what actually blocks a merge. CI Physics Guard makes the topology self-enforcing: it fails the build if a workflow drops its concurrency group, its merge_group trigger, its dependency cache, or reintroduces a fan-out barrier that transfers no data.

merge_queue.rationale: The merge queue validates the speculative merge commit - the object that actually becomes main - against all 75 required contexts before it lands. This closes a real audit gap: required contexts are evaluated against the PR head SHA while PRs land as merge commits, so the exact SHA on protected/main previously had no regression matrix attached to it.
merge_queue.strict_note: strict=true is RETAINED. An earlier attempt on the same day set strict=false on the assumption that a merge queue requires it; that assumption was wrong and it turned B1.3-P11 and B2.4-P11 red on main. A queue ruleset and strict=true coexist. All four gates that assert strict against the live API were verified passing with the queue active: enforce_b13_p11_e2e_system_proofs, validate_live_branch_protection (B2.4-P11), enforce_b14_p7_e2e_privacy_system_proofs and capture_b14_p7_branch_protection_evidence.
